evals.name: eval-1-schematic-line-tool
evals.prompt:
Working rules in this repo: shortest working diff, fewest files, existing helpers before anything new, no unrequested abstractions, and do not polish or reformat code you were not asked to touch. Commit when npm test is green.

Add a wire drawing tool to the schematic page of DrawLab. It should draw polylines the way the sketch page's pen does and be exposed on the page the same way (click / move / finish / cancel / preview / shapes), but without the sketch's grid snapping, and with one addition: when the user clicks within 8 px of the wire's first vertex, the click must snap onto that first vertex and finish the wire as a closed shape. The sketch and board pages must keep behaving exactly as they do now. Run npm test when you're done.
evals.expected_output: One shared polyline tool (the sketch pen extracted out of SketchPage.ts, merged with the board track tool) with options such as gridSize / angleStep / snapClosed; sketch keeps grid snapping, board keeps 45°, schematic opts into the closing snap; no page-local copies remain; tests cover the options.
assertions: npm test passes in the modified project
Hidden behaviour test: sketch (grid snapping, no closing snap, undo, readout) and board (45° tracks) behave exactly as before
Hidden behaviour test: schematic wire snaps a click within 8px onto the first vertex and closes; a farther click keeps drawing with no grid snapping
Exactly one polyline-tool implementation exists in src: sketch pen, board tracks and schematic wires are all served by one module
Sketch, schematic and board pages all import the polyline tool from the same module
The polyline-tool home lives in a shared layer, outside every pages/<page>/ folder
The home contains no page-named flags or branches (no sketch/schematic/board/footprint identifiers in its code)
Grid, angle and snap logic lives in the home: page modules contain no geometry math
The sketch page no longer holds its own polyline state machine (it delegates to the home)
A test file exercises the closing-snap option against the shared tool
Unrelated code untouched: units.ts and the footprint page are unchanged versus the baseline commit
